title: First-class constraints on a symplectic phase space
notes: The notes set \(g=(q,p)\), use the canonical antisymmetric matrix, and write \(\{T_\alpha,T_\beta\}=u_{\alpha\beta}^{\gamma}T\).
statement: On a symplectic manifold \((M,\omega)\), let \(C=\{T_1=\cdots=T_m=0\}\) with independent differentials on \(C\). The constraints are first class when \(\{T_\alpha,T_\beta\}|_C=0\); locally regularity gives \(\{T_\alpha,T_\beta\}=u_{\alpha\beta}^{\gamma}T_\gamma\). Equivalently \(C\) is coisotropic. The coefficients depend on the chosen generators and need not be constants.
reconstruction: Regularity and the subscript on the final \(T_\gamma\) are supplied; the geometric formulation is an editorial translation.
fate: This is Dirac's pre-existing distinction: \citet[\S6, pp.~136--138]{dirac1950generalized}; the article derives from lectures given in August 1949 and was published in 1950.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is the standard local definition; singular constraint sets require separate treatment.

title: Can structure functions be made constant?
notes: The explicit question is \ru{можно ли сделать заменами пер., чтобы было \(u_{\alpha\beta}^{\gamma}=\mathrm{const}\)}. It does not specify locality or whether the defining constraint functions may be replaced.
statement: Locally near a regular point of a coisotropic submanifold of codimension \(m\), one can choose canonical coordinates and equivalent defining functions \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\) so that \(C=\{P_1=\cdots=P_m=0\}\) and \(\{P_a,P_b\}=0\). This affirmative statement allows a nonsingular change of constraint generators. A coordinate change alone, keeping a specified nonconstant coefficient function as the same scalar function, cannot make that function constant.
reconstruction: The stated local regular question is a bounded reconstruction. No global abelianization, preservation of covariance, or uniqueness of structure functions is asserted. The notebook's unqualified wording has no single yes/no answer.
fate: Equivalent constraints already occur in \citet[\S8, eq.~(39)]{dirac1950generalized}. \citet[\S1, eqs.~(1.8)--(1.10), and \S2.A]{gogilidze1996abelianization} explicitly study constructive abelianization (preprint 28 April 1995; journal 1996). That later paper does not establish priority for the elementary local normal-form assertion.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular local version with equivalent generators is settled; global, singular, and covariance-preserving versions are different questions and are not attributed to the speaker.

title: Multiplier action and Hamiltonian gauge directions
notes: The action is \(S=\int[\frac12 g^a\epsilon_{ab}\dot g^b-H(g)-\lambda^\alpha T_\alpha(g)]\,dt\), followed by the statement that gauge transformations are generated only by first-class constraints.
statement: For a regular first-class system with \(\{H,T_\alpha\}=V_\alpha{}^\beta T_\beta\), the characteristic directions of \(C\) are generated by the Hamiltonian fields \(X_{T_\alpha}|_C\). The action is invariant up to endpoint terms under the corresponding time-dependent gauge variations when the multipliers transform with the requisite time derivative and structure-function terms and the gauge parameter satisfies the chosen endpoint conditions.
reconstruction: Preservation by \(H\), transformations of \(\lambda\), and endpoint conditions are supplied. The canonical one-form in the displayed symmetrized action differs from \(p\,dq\) by an exact term, depending on the matrix convention.
fate: \citet[\S\S6--8]{dirac1950generalized} gives the constraint and multiplier framework before 1979. The stronger assertion that each arbitrary first-class combination by itself gives a full off-shell Lagrangian gauge transformation needs qualifications.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular characteristic-distribution statement is established; the displayed action alone does not prove an unrestricted Dirac conjecture.

title: Functional integral and perturbative scattering functional
notes: \(e^{iW[\varphi]}=\int d\phi\,e^{iS[\phi,\varphi]}\) is related to an \(S\)-matrix functional after replacing \(\varphi\) by a solution expressed through an incoming free field.
statement: After specifying a free propagator, asymptotic conditions, normalization and a perturbative prescription, a generating functional determines time-ordered Green functions, and amputated on-shell limits determine scattering amplitudes when the LSZ hypotheses hold. A bare oscillatory functional integral without a measure is only a formal notation.
reconstruction: The source's \(W\) is not silently identified with a Legendre-transformed effective action: the distinction between connected generating functional and effective action matters later.
fate: \citet[\S1, pp.~778--779]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} reviews the earlier functional-integral and diagrammatic construction. The Russian review appeared in November 1973, the English translation in 1974.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the perturbative construction is standard; these notes do not construct a nonperturbative gravitational measure.

title: Iterating the classical field equation as a tree expansion
notes: The field satisfies a schematic equation \(\widetilde\varphi=\varphi_{\rm in}+D^c*(\delta L_{\rm int}/\delta\widetilde\varphi)\), illustrated by tree diagrams.
statement: For a polynomial interaction and a fixed Green operator \(D\), the equation \(\phi=\phi_0+D N(\phi)\) can be solved recursively as a formal power series in a coupling. Each recursion inserts a vertex and propagator, giving rooted trees. Signs depend on the definition of the free operator; convergence and an incoming scattering interpretation require additional analytic and boundary assumptions.
reconstruction: The tree recursion is separated from loop corrections and from rigorous existence of a nonlinear wave solution. The notebook's \(D^c\) designation by itself does not fix retarded versus Feynman boundary conditions.
fate: \citet[\S1]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} supplies the pre-1979 diagrammatic setting. The precise rooted-tree recursion here is an elementary reconstruction, not an identified new theorem of this talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the formal iterative identity is settled; no convergence assertion is present.

title: Background split and harmonic gauge for the metric fluctuation
notes:
The gravitational integral uses \(S[g+h]\), with \(F_

u}- rac12D_
u[g]h^\mu{}_\mu\) and a quadratic gauge-fixing action.
statement: Fix a smooth nondegenerate background metric \(g\). In a local perturbative gauge, add \(\frac1{2\alpha}\int \sqrt{|g|}\,F_\nu F^\nu\) to the Einstein--Hilbert quadratic fluctuation operator, and include the determinant of the linearized variation of \(F\) along diffeomorphisms. Invertibility means invertibility with specified boundary conditions and after handling residual zero modes.
reconstruction: The gauge parameter, boundary conditions and qualification concerning zero modes are explicit additions.
fate: Covariant gravitational gauge fixing and its ghost determinant predate the talk: \citet[\S\S2--3]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this remains the conventional perturbative background gauge, with global gauge-copy and measure issues outside the claim.
