title: Additional ghost interactions in supergravity
notes: The text says that one further term suffices in supergravity whereas an arbitrary theory requires infinitely many corrections.
statement: For a gauge algebra that closes only modulo field equations, the naive determinant-only Faddeev--Popov rules need additional terms. Particular supergravity formulations admit quartic ghost interactions. No precise model, auxiliary-field content or bound on ghost degree is recorded, so the universal one-term/infinitely-many contrast is not a determinate theorem.
fate: \citet[pp.~141--152]{kallosh1978modified} is the contemporaneous 1978 publication lead; its publisher abstract and metadata were found but the full article was inaccessible. \citet[\S2.2 and introduction]{fuster2005brst} later distinguishes open algebras and the antifield formalism. It does not turn this 1979 remark into a statement of the later BV master-equation theory.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the general open-algebra framework is established, but the notebook's asserted truncation cannot be verified without a specified supergravity model.

title: Diffeomorphism invariance and background covariance
notes: Equations (9)--(12) compare \(S[g+\delta g]\), \(W[g+\delta g]\), and the induced change of the fluctuation \(h\).
statement: Einstein--Hilbert action is invariant under diffeomorphisms compatible with boundary data. Simultaneous background and fluctuation transformations can preserve a background-covariant gauge-fixed formal integral if the measure, determinant and regularization preserve that symmetry. Infinitesimal equality is understood to first order in the parameter.
reconstruction: Background covariance is kept distinct from independence of the choice of gauge-fixing function.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--3]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} provides the pre-existing covariant construction. Modern BRST qualifications concerning the measure and anomalies are explicit in \citet[\S\S7--9]{fuster2005brst}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the classical identity is exact under its boundary hypotheses; a quantum version requires anomaly-free symmetry preservation.

title: On-shell gauge independence and its loop-order restriction
notes: After subtracting \(S[g]\) and its linear fluctuation term, the variation of the radiative functional is proportional to \(\delta S/\delta g\); the notes conclude independence on the classical shell.
statement: BRST variation yields a gauge-parameter identity of the form \(\delta\Gamma=\Gamma_{,i}K^i\) for the properly defined effective action. Consequently its value at a quantum stationary point is gauge independent. At one loop \(\Gamma=S+\hbar\Gamma_1+\cdots\), the corresponding variation of \(\Gamma_1\) vanishes on the classical shell \(S_{,i}=0\).
reconstruction: The effective-action interpretation, loop expansion and distinction between the classical and quantum shell are supplied. The displayed notebook formula is treated as a schematic first-order identity; the later Higgs-background treatment checks the principle, not every gravity-specific detail.
fate: \citet[pp.~173--188]{nielsen1975gauge} is the 1975 original publication lead, checked indirectly. The explicitly read primary later treatment \citet[\S2.1, eq.~(1)]{espinosa2015higgstory} states the effective-action identity and its quantum-stationary consequence. The one-loop classical-shell consequence follows by expanding that identity consistently in \(\hbar\). Neither source permits classical and quantum equations of motion to be identified at all orders.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, on-shell gauge independence is established within the BRST perturbative hypotheses; off-shell effective actions generally depend on gauge.

title: Changing a gauge-fixing functional by a change of variables
notes: The proof varies a quadratic gauge form \(F\) and compensates by \(h\mapsto h+\delta h\). An expectation of \(\delta h\) is written without its insertion, and equation (20) has an unmatched factor \(1/2\).
statement: In a finite-dimensional regular gauge model, an admissible local gauge slice has an invertible derivative along gauge orbits. A change of slice can then be compensated locally, with its Jacobian included. In a formal field integral, the same manipulation requires a regulated measure, appropriate boundaries and consistent normalization. Invertibility of a quadratic fluctuation form alone does not prove global gauge independence.
reconstruction: The elementary change-of-variables conditions replace the notebook's unrestricted functional-integral claim. The flawed equality is not used as a proof.
fate: \citet[\S8]{fuster2005brst} states the BRST gauge-independence argument in a modern form; \citet[\S\S2--3]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} gives its earlier determinant setting. Neither validates the two literal misprints.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the local/formal argument is standard; a nonperturbative global statement is not established by these formulas.

title: Maxwell gauge invariance and its Hessian kernel
notes: \(S[A]=-\frac14\int(\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu)^2\) is invariant under \(A_\mu\mapsto A_\mu+\partial_\mu\xi\); the Hessian is degenerate.
statement:
For a flat background and suitable compact support or boundary conditions, \(F=dA\) is unchanged by \(A\mapsto A+d\xi\). The quadratic operator \(K_{\mu
u}=\eta_{\mu
u}\Box-\partial_\mu\partial_
u\) satisfies \(K_{\mu
u}\partial^
u\xi=0\), so no inverse exists before removing gauge directions.
fate: This is the Abelian special case of the earlier gauge-action construction; compare \citet[eqs.~(1)--(6)]{yangmills1954conservation}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the algebraic kernel identity is elementary and unchanged; boundary conditions determine residual modes.

title: Lorenz and generalized linear gauges for electromagnetism
notes: The two examples add \((\partial\cdot A)^2/(2\alpha)\) and \((\partial\cdot A+\beta n\cdot A)^2/(2\alpha)\).
statement: A linear gauge functional \(F(A)=L^\mu A_\mu\) produces a quadratic gauge-fixing term. For Abelian transformations its Faddeev--Popov operator is \(L^\mu\partial_\mu\), independent of \(A\), and the ghosts decouple when that operator and its boundary prescription are fixed. Gauge parameters must avoid singular gauges or require a separate limiting prescription.
reconstruction: The fixed vector \(n\), residual gauge kernel and parameter restrictions are specified; the notes do not prove equivalence for every \(\alpha,\beta\).
fate: \citet[\S\S1--3]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} reviews the determinant construction for which Maxwell theory is the linear case.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the two expressions are standard admissible local gauge choices when the corresponding operator can be inverted.

title: Sources and time-ordered correlation functions
notes: The notes define \(Z(J)=c\int e^{iW[\varphi]+iJ\varphi}\,d\mu(\varphi)\) and identify source derivatives with products of fields.
statement: With \(\hbar=1\) and normalization \(Z(0)=1\), the formal time-ordered \(n\)-point function is \(i^{-n}\delta^n Z/\delta J(x_1)\cdots\delta J(x_n)|_{J=0}\). For non-normalized \(Z\), divide by \(Z(0)\). Derivatives of \(-i\log Z\) generate connected functions with the corresponding powers of \(i\).
reconstruction: The missing factors, evaluation at zero source and normalization are stated explicitly. No measure-existence assertion is added.
fate: The construction is reviewed before the seminar in \citet[\S1]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}, Russian 1973/English 1974.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is a formal or suitably constructed generating-functional identity, not a proof of existence of an interacting quantum field theory.

title: Coupling expansion versus expansion around a classical solution
notes: A scalar \(\varphi^4\) example precedes two schemes: a coupling expansion and stationary phase near a solution. The notebook says the first is inapplicable to gravity and writes a dot on \(\varphi\) in the mass term.
statement: For a scalar field the conventional action has a kinetic term, a mass term \(m^2\varphi^2/2\), and a quartic interaction. Coupling expansion and an \(\hbar\)-expansion about a saddle are distinct formal organizations; both can be used in perturbative gravity after gauge fixing. Nonrenormalizability by power counting does not make every coupling expansion undefined.
reconstruction: The mass-term emendation and the distinction between perturbative definability and renormalizability are editorial.
fate: \citet[\S\S1--2]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} explicitly presents perturbation theory for gravity before 1979 and therefore rules out the blanket prohibition.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the two expansions are standard; the printed mass term and absolute prohibition need correction.

title: Nondegenerate stationary phase and its missing normalization
notes: The notes approximate an oscillatory integral by the inverse square root of the Hessian determinant and a value at a stationary point.
statement: For real \(S\in C^\infty\), \(a\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\), and a unique nondegenerate critical point \(x_0\) in the relevant support, as \(\hbar\downarrow0\), \(\int e^{iS(x)/\hbar}a(x)\,dx=e^{iS(x_0)/\hbar}(2\pi\hbar)^{n/2}e^{i\pi\operatorname{sgn}S''(x_0)/4}|\det S''(x_0)|^{-1/2}[a(x_0)+O(\hbar)]\). Multiple critical points contribute a sum; a critical manifold requires a different theorem.
reconstruction: Amplitude, support, nondegeneracy, absolute determinant, signature phase and power of \(2\pi\hbar\) are supplied. The generic remainder is \(O(\hbar)\), not the notebook's stronger small-o assertion.
fate: The finite-dimensional Gaussian basis of the earlier path-integral method is given in \citet[\S1]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}. The precise stationary-phase statement here is a classical mathematical reconstruction, not a new result identified with this lecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the finite-dimensional theorem is settled; it does not justify an infinite-dimensional gravity saddle expansion without further work.

title: Gauge degeneracy obstructs the naive saddle formula
notes: For Maxwell theory the Hessian annihilates gradients, and integration along a gauge orbit is described as producing a group-volume factor.
statement:
If \(S\) is invariant under a smooth group action, its Hessian at a critical point annihilates infinitesimal orbit directions. Thus the isolated nondegenerate stationary-phase formula cannot be applied in those directions. For Maxwell theory the identity is \((\eta_{\mu
u}\Box-\partial_\mu\partial_
u)\partial^
u\xi=0\).
fate: This is the obstruction addressed by the earlier Faddeev--Popov construction; \citet[\S2]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the degeneracy statement is exact; an infinite group volume is a formal description unless a quotient measure is defined.

title: Infinitesimal group generators, Lie equations and invariant measures
notes: A transformation \(g\mapsto f(g,\theta)\), generators \(R_\alpha^a\), structure constants and a matrix \(\lambda(\theta)\) are introduced. Divergence-free generators are associated with a \ru{унимодулярная} group.
statement: For a smooth Lie-group action, the derivatives of \(f\) along group coordinates factor through fundamental vector fields and a Maurer--Cartan frame. A density \(\rho\,dg\) is invariant precisely when \(\partial_a(\rho R_\alpha^a)=0\). This is an action-and-density condition. Unimodularity of the abstract group means its left and right Haar measures agree and is not equivalent to \(\partial_aR_\alpha^a=0\) in arbitrary coordinates on the acted-on manifold.
reconstruction: The density and the distinction between group unimodularity and volume preservation of a particular action are supplied.
fate: The invariant-measure requirement is part of the pre-existing gauge argument; compare \citet[\S2]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}. \citet[\S~II]{bering1997geometry} later makes its geometric measure assumptions explicit (1997 preprint, revised 1998).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the Lie-action identities are standard; the notebook's terminology should not be used as an equivalence theorem.

title: An admissible local gauge slice
notes: The condition \(\psi^\alpha(f(g,\theta))=0\) is required to have one solution \(\theta\) for every \(g\); the notes call this a section.
statement: For a locally free action of an \(m\)-dimensional Lie group, \(m\) gauge functions define a local slice when \(M^\alpha{}_\beta(g)=d\psi^\alpha_g(R_\beta(g))\) is invertible on the slice. The inverse-function theorem then gives local uniqueness near a chosen intersection. Global existence and uniqueness require additional assumptions and generally fail in non-Abelian gauge theory.
reconstruction: Local uniqueness is substituted for the universal global section that the notes assume rather than prove.
fate: The local determinant method predates 1979. The global obstruction is the topic of \citet[pp.~1--19]{gribov1978quantization}, published in 1978, but that original text was not recovered in this audit. The independently read later primary analysis \citet[\S~II]{bering1997geometry} explicitly excludes global Gribov problems from its gauge-independence argument.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, local slices remain useful; a universal global slice is not available in general.

title: Faddeev--Popov determinant identity
notes: Equations (21)--(27) derive \(1=\int\delta(\psi(f(g,\theta)))\Delta_\psi(f(g,\theta))\,d\sigma(\theta)\), with \(\Delta_\psi=\det(\psi_{,a}R^a)\). Equation (23) omits \(f\) in one argument.
statement: If the orbit-to-gauge map has exactly one regular zero in the integration chart, the ordinary real delta-function change-of-variables formula gives \(1=\int \delta^m(\psi(f(g,\theta)))|\det \partial_\theta\psi(f(g,\theta))|\,d^m\theta\). With a consistently oriented formal measure one uses the signed determinant. The group-coordinate Jacobian converts this to the Haar-measure form.
reconstruction: The absolute value for positive measures, possible orientation convention and unique-zero hypothesis are supplied. Equation (23)'s argument must be \(f(g,\theta)\).
fate: \citet[\S2]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} gives the earlier determinant insertion. The local real-variable identity explains exactly which regularity and multiplicity conditions are needed.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the local change-of-variables identity is settled; multiple gauge intersections change the naive formula.

title: Factoring gauge volume from an invariant integral
notes: The invariant integrand and measure are changed by \(g\mapsto f(g,\theta)\), producing a common gauge-volume factor and a reduced delta-function integral.
statement: For a free proper action with compatible measures and convergent integrals, disintegration along orbits yields a quotient integral and the orbit-volume factor. In the formal field-theoretic version, common infinite gauge volumes are canceled only after a specified normalization; insertion of the determinant and compatible gauge slice is essential.
reconstruction: The honest finite-dimensional hypotheses are supplied. The notes' repeated \(d\sigma\) in an integral over field coordinates is a variable-label error, not a new measure.
fate: The preceding reduction is the pre-1979 Faddeev--Popov method; \citet[\S2]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the geometric quotient construction is standard where its hypotheses hold; cancellation of divergent factors alone is not a proof.

title: Gauge averaging and the indispensable normalization
notes: The slice is moved to \(\psi(g)=c\), averaged with \(e^{i\Omega(c)}dc\), and equation (40) divides by \(\int e^{i\Omega(c)}dc\). The next displayed equality drops this denominator.
statement: If \(I(c)\) is independent of the admissible slice value \(c\), then \(\int w(c)I(c)\,dc/\int w(c)\,dc=I\), provided the denominator is nonzero and integrals or their regularized meanings exist. Taking \(w=e^{i\Omega}\) gives a gauge-fixing action but not an unnormalized gauge-independent partition function.
reconstruction: The distinction between the normalized quotient and the raw averaged integral is explicit.
fate: This is the normalization step in the earlier covariant gauge procedure; \citet[\S3]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the normalized identity is elementary; equation (41) needs the factor already present in equation (40).

title: Grassmann representation of the gauge determinant
notes: The determinant \(\det(\psi_{,a}R^a)\) is represented using anticommuting \(\xi,\bar\xi\), producing \(W_{\rm eff}=W+\Omega(\psi)+\bar\xi\,\psi_{,a}R^a\xi\).
statement: For an \(m\times m\) matrix \(M\), a fixed Berezin integration order gives \(\int d\bar c\,dc\,e^{-\bar cMc}=\det M\). In an oscillatory convention \(e^{i\bar cMc}\), the harmless factor \(i^m\) is absorbed in normalization. Ghost parity is opposite to the gauge-parameter parity; fermionic gauge directions require commuting ghosts.
reconstruction: Finite-dimensional normalization and the graded qualification are supplied; the general fermionic extension is not claimed to have been read in the inaccessible 1978 article.
fate: \citet[\S3, following eq.~(3.21)]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} uses the determinant representation. The graded first/second-class extension is the pre-1979 lead \citet[pp.~343--348]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the finite-dimensional Berezin identity is exact; its functional-integral use remains subject to the chosen regularization.

title: BRST transformations and the antighost qualification
notes: Equations (43)--(46) give \(\delta g^a=R_\alpha^a\xi^\alpha\mu\), \(\delta\xi^\alpha=\frac12t^\alpha_{\beta\gamma}\xi^\beta\xi^\gamma\mu\), and \(\delta\bar\xi_\alpha=\Omega_{,\alpha}(\psi)\mu\), with odd constant \(\mu\).
statement: For a closed Lie gauge algebra, \(s\phi=R_\alpha c^\alpha\), \(sc^\alpha=-\frac12f^\alpha_{\beta\gamma}c^\beta c^\gamma\) define a nilpotent odd derivation with consistent left/right conventions. Add an auxiliary field \(b_\alpha\) and set \(s\bar c_\alpha=b_\alpha,\ sb_\alpha=0\) for off-shell nilpotence. Eliminating \(b\) by its equation yields the notebook's gauge-function variation, whose antighost nilpotence is generally only on shell.
reconstruction: Signs are translated from the notebook's right odd parameter. The auxiliary field is a modern clarification, not a field visibly introduced in this passage.
fate: The original development was publicly announced in 1974 and appears in the April 1975 report \citet[\S\S2--3]{becchirouetstora1975renormalization}; \citet[\S6, eqs.~(6.1)--(6.5)]{fuster2005brst} makes the auxiliary-field formulation explicit.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the BRST construction is established; nilpotence of the displayed antighost rule requires the stated on-shell qualification.

title: Chevalley--Eilenberg cancellation behind BRST nilpotence
notes: The notes introduce \(\Gamma_\alpha=R_\alpha^a\partial_a\), compute \((\Gamma_\alpha\xi^\alpha)^2\), and cancel it using the ghost transformation.
statement: If \([\Gamma_\alpha,\Gamma_\beta]=f_{\alpha\beta}^\gamma\Gamma_\gamma\), then \(s=c^\alpha\Gamma_\alpha-\frac12f_{\alpha\beta}^{\gamma}c^\alpha c^\beta\partial/\partial c^\gamma\) satisfies \(s^2=0\). The representation identity and Jacobi identity give the cancellations; this statement applies to a closed Lie algebra action, not automatically to field-dependent or on-shell closing algebras.
reconstruction: The operator is written with a single left-derivative convention. Structure functions require the corresponding more general resolution.
fate: The pre-1979 BRST report \citet[\S2]{becchirouetstora1975renormalization} presents this algebraic mechanism; \citet[\S4]{fuster2005brst} relates it to cohomology.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the nilpotence identity is exact under the closed-algebra assumptions.

title: Physical unitarity and cancellation of ghost states
notes: The notes discuss a unitary \(S\)-operator, internal ghosts, and cancellations leaving physical particles.
statement: In an anomaly-free perturbative BRST theory, the conserved nilpotent charge defines physical states through its cohomology. If the induced inner product is positive and unphysical states form canceling sectors, the \(S\)-operator induced on physical cohomology is unitary. The enlarged ghost state space itself need not have a positive-definite inner product.
reconstruction: The physical quotient and positivity assumptions prevent the bare symbolic equality from being interpreted as a universal Hilbert-space theorem.
fate: \citet[\S3, pp.~29--39 and abstract]{becchirouetstora1975renormalization} proves physical unitarity and gauge-parameter independence for its specified massive Higgs-model setting, not for every conceivable gauge theory.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, physical perturbative unitarity is established for standard anomaly-free models; the notes do not settle global or nonperturbative unitarity of supergravity.

title: Field-dependent BRST parameters and gauge independence
notes: A field-dependent odd parameter involving \(\bar\xi\,\delta\psi\) is used to cancel a change of gauge; Slavnov identities are mentioned.
statement: An infinitesimal change of gauge fermion changes the BRST-exact gauge-fixing action. A BRST change of integration variables, with its super-Jacobian included, leaves expectation values of BRST-closed observables unchanged when the measure is BRST invariant, boundary terms vanish, and the integration domain is admissible. A field-dependent parameter generally has a nontrivial Jacobian even if a constant BRST transformation preserves the measure.
reconstruction: The measure/domain qualifications and the distinction between constant and field-dependent parameters are made explicit.
fate: The earlier BRST report \citet[\S3, pp.~29--34]{becchirouetstora1975renormalization} provides the gauge-independence identities; \citet[\S V, eqs.~(V.8)--(V.9)]{bering1997geometry} explicitly treats the later geometric gauge-fixing argument and its endpoint condition.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the formal gauge-independence theorem is standard with these hypotheses; it is not a proof that gauge copies or anomalies cannot occur.

title: Open supergravity algebras
notes: The lecture says supergravity is \ru{не группа}, in contrast with the preceding Yang--Mills derivation.
statement: The identifiable mathematical content is that commutators of gauge transformations in some supergravity formulations close only modulo equations of motion, or have field-dependent coefficients. This is an open gauge algebra. It is not the assertion that no groupoid, integrated symmetry or auxiliary-field formulation can exist.
reconstruction: Open-algebra terminology is supplied. The notes do not specify which supergravity or auxiliary fields are intended.
fate: \citet[pp.~141--152]{kallosh1978modified} is a pre-talk lead; \citet[\S2.2]{fuster2005brst} verifies the later precise distinction. The original 1978 full text was not accessed.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the distinction is established, but no model-specific closure identity can be recovered from this sentence.

title: Yang--Mills curvature, infinitesimal gauge generator and ghosts
notes: The final example takes a compact semisimple group, \(F=dA+[A,A]\), a Lorenz gauge, and a ghost term \(-(\partial_\mu\bar\xi)D^\mu\xi\). Equation (60) abbreviates the functional generator.
statement: For a connection \(A\) on a fixed bundle and invariant inner product on its compact semisimple Lie algebra, \(F_A=dA+\frac12[A,A]\) and \(\delta_\epsilon A=D_A\epsilon\). In a local Lorenz gauge the Faddeev--Popov operator is \(\partial^\mu D_\mu\), with ghost action represented after integration by parts. As a distributional kernel, \(R_{\mu\,b}^{a}(x,y)=D_{\mu\,b}^{a}(x)\delta(x-y)\); the delta function and spacetime index cannot be dropped in a literal kernel equation.
reconstruction: Bundle, contraction, boundary and kernel conventions are supplied; the gauge parameter's reciprocal can be absorbed by renaming it.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(1)--(11)]{yangmills1954conservation} supplies the classical 1954 model; \citet[\S2]{becchirouetstora1975renormalization} gives its pre-1979 ghost and BRST extension.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the classical and perturbative construction is standard; a rigorous four-dimensional continuum quantum theory is a separate problem.

title: Difficulties in operator and canonical approaches to gravity
notes: A heading promises three approaches; the written enumeration discusses operator-valued metrics and a Hamiltonian splitting \(M^3\times\mathbb R\). Metric contraction and covariance/topology are raised as difficulties.
statement: No theorem with quantified hypotheses is stated. A Hamiltonian formulation chooses suitable spacelike hypersurfaces and imposes gravitational constraints; this restricts the geometric setting and does not by itself prove incompatibility with diffeomorphism invariance. Operator-valued metric contractions require an ordering and regularization prescription.
reconstruction: The unwritten third enumerated approach is not invented. The statement distinguishes methodological questions from an impossibility theorem.
fate: \citet[\S1]{gibbonshawking1977action} supplies the path-integral context explicitly named by the notebook. It is a thematic match, not a publication of Gelfand's informal assessment.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the notes do not specify a uniquely identifiable obstruction theorem or research problem.

title: Einstein equation from the action and the stress tensor normalization
notes: The notes vary \((16\pi G)^{-1}\int(R-2\Lambda)\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x+\int L_m\sqrt{-g}\,d^4x\), but the displayed definition of \(T_{ab}\) has a factor \(-\frac12\sqrt{-g}\) and varies with respect to \(g_{ab}\).
statement: Let \(S_m[g,\phi]\) be the matter action and define \(T_{ab}=-2(-g)^{-1/2}\delta S_m/\delta g^{ab}\). With fixed boundary data and the requisite gravitational boundary term, metric stationarity gives \(R_{ab}-\frac12Rg_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=8\pi G\,T_{ab}\). Equivalently \(T^{ab}=2(-g)^{-1/2}\delta S_m/\delta g_{ab}\).
reconstruction: The distinction between \(L_m\), its volume density and the integrated matter action, and the inverse-metric variation are supplied.
fate: The variational action and its boundary qualification are explicit in \citet[\S II, eq.~(2.1)]{gibbonshawking1977action}, published 15 May 1977; receipt on 4 October 1976 is not evidence of a public preprint.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected variational equation is standard; the notebook's stress-tensor normalization cannot be retained as a definition of the displayed Einstein equation.

title: What Yau's theorem actually says
notes: The page attributes to Yau existence and uniqueness of an Einstein metric on a compact Kähler manifold with \(\Lambda\ne0\).
statement: On a compact Kähler manifold, any real closed \((1,1)\)-form representing \(2\pi c_1(X)\) is the Ricci form of a unique Kähler metric in each fixed Kähler class. For \(c_1(X)=0\) this yields a unique Ricci-flat metric in each class. If \(c_1(X)<0\), there is a uniquely normalized negative Kähler--Einstein metric. Compact Kähler manifolds with positive \(c_1\) need not admit a Kähler--Einstein metric; arbitrary compact Kähler manifolds do not satisfy the notebook's claim.
reconstruction: The sign of the first Chern class, prescribed Ricci form, fixed Kähler class and normalization are all essential emendations.
fate: \citet[Theorem~1, p.~1798]{yau1977calabi} announced the corrected results in May 1977; the full proof appeared in \citet[pp.~339--411]{yau1978ricci} in 1978. The announcement credits Aubin in the negative case. Neither asserts universal \(\Lambda\ne0\) existence.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, these corrected theorems remain established. The notes' unrestricted uniqueness is not an open problem.

title: Gibbons--Hawking boundary term and gluing
notes: The action acquires \((8\pi)^{-1}\int_{\partial M}K\sqrt{-h}\), motivated by boundary variation and an additivity relation denoted \(I[g_1+g_2]=I[g_1]+I[g_2]\).
statement: For a smooth non-null boundary and fixed induced metric, the Einstein--Hilbert action needs the extrinsic-curvature boundary term, with sign determined by signature and outward-normal conventions, to cancel normal derivatives of the metric variation. When two regions are glued smoothly along a common hypersurface, their opposite normals cancel the interface terms. Corners or nonsmooth gluing require additional analysis.
reconstruction: \(g_1+g_2\) is interpreted as gluing regions carrying metrics, not adding two metric tensors. Smoothness and the absence of corners are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S II, eq.~(2.1) and p.~2753]{gibbonshawking1977action} gives the 1977 Dirichlet boundary prescription.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the boundary term is standard; the literal tensor-addition interpretation of the notebook notation is invalid.

title: Reference subtraction for an asymptotically flat action
notes: The boundary integrand is changed from \(K\) to \(K-K_0\), with \(K_0\) associated to a comparison geometry.
statement: For a chosen asymptotically flat reference and compatible induced boundary geometry, subtracting its extrinsic-curvature contribution fixes the zero of the action and can render the limit finite. A function of the fixed induced boundary metric may be added without changing the bulk Dirichlet variational equation. Existence or uniqueness of a reference embedding is not automatic for every boundary.
reconstruction: The asymptotically flat comparison and fixed-boundary conditions prevent a universal reference-subtraction theorem from being attributed to the notes.
fate: \citet[\S II, p.~2753, before eq.~(2.2)]{gibbonshawking1977action} explicitly chooses the subtraction to make the flat-space action vanish.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, reference subtraction is established in its stated setting; its geometric choices remain part of the prescription.

title: Even graded canonical Poisson bracket
notes: Coordinates are assigned parities, and equations (1)--(4) give a canonical bracket, graded antisymmetry and the graded Jacobi identity.
statement: On an even symplectic supermanifold with homogeneous canonical coordinate pairs of equal parity, the Poisson bracket has parity \(\epsilon(f)+\epsilon(g)\), obeys \(\{f,g\}=-(-1)^{\epsilon(f)\epsilon(g)}\{g,f\}\), the graded Leibniz rule and graded Jacobi identity. Left/right derivatives must be used consistently. In particular the bracket of two odd functions is symmetric.
reconstruction: The bracket here is even; it is not the later odd BV antibracket. Coordinate signs are restated invariantly rather than silently copied between incompatible derivative conventions.
fate: The boson/fermion constraint extension was published before the seminar in \citet[pp.~343--348]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}. Its detailed sign conventions remain an indirectly checked publication lead.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, even symplectic supergeometry supplies the standard mathematical interpretation.

title: First and second class: why determinant zero is insufficient
notes: \(Q_{\alpha\beta}=\{T_\alpha,T_\beta\}\) is introduced; nonzero determinant is labeled second class, whereas determinant zero together with a Hamiltonian condition is labeled first class.
statement: For independent constraints, second class means that the full constraint bracket matrix is invertible on the constraint surface; in the graded setting use the appropriate even supermatrix and Berezinian. A function is first class if its bracket with every constraint vanishes on that surface. A degenerate \(Q\) can contain both first- and second-class directions, so \(\det Q=0\) does not imply that all listed constraints are first class.
reconstruction: Regularity, weak equality and the distinction between degeneracy and complete first-class closure are supplied.
fate: \citet[\S\S6--8]{dirac1950generalized} already distinguishes mixed systems and changes of constraint basis; \citet[pp.~343--348]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization} is the graded extension lead.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected classification is standard; a rank test must be supplemented by the full bracket structure.

title: Constrained stationary action and Lagrange multipliers
notes: A constrained Hamiltonian action is replaced by an unconstrained action with multipliers \(\lambda^\alpha T_\alpha\).
statement: For smooth independent constraints and variations with fixed compatible endpoints, stationarity on the constraint submanifold is equivalent locally to stationarity of the multiplier action together with \(T_\alpha=0\). Constraint preservation imposes \(\dot T_\alpha=\{T_\alpha,H\}+\lambda^\beta\{T_\alpha,T_\beta\}=0\); it may determine multipliers or generate further constraints.
reconstruction: Independence and the possibility of secondary constraints are essential; singular constraints need not admit this elementary equivalence.
fate: \citet[\S\S2--6]{dirac1950generalized} develops the multiplier consistency algorithm before 1979.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular multiplier statement is settled.

title: Dirac bracket for second-class constraints
notes: The inverse matrix \(Q^{-1}\) is inserted into a corrected bracket, and constraints then bracket to zero.
statement: In the ordinary even case, \(\{f,g\}_D=\{f,g\}-\{f,T_\alpha\}(Q^{-1})^{\alpha\beta}\{T_\beta,g\}\). It is a Poisson bracket wherever \(Q\) is invertible and satisfies \(\{T_\alpha,f\}_D=0\). Its restriction to the constraint surface is independent of extensions of the restricted functions. The super version uses the corresponding graded contractions.
reconstruction: An unambiguous ordinary-even formula is stated first; graded sign factors depend on the source's derivative convention.
fate: \citet[\S8, eqs.~(34)--(38), and appendix]{dirac1950generalized} gives the construction and Jacobi verification in 1950.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the Dirac reduction bracket is established on the regular second-class locus.

title: Gelfand's geometric interpretation of the Dirac bracket
notes: Gelfand identifies the construction with restricting a nondegenerate skew form to the constraint surface and inverting it there.
statement: For a symplectic manifold \((M,\omega)\), the regular second-class surface \(C\) is symplectic: \(\iota^*\omega\) is nondegenerate. Its inverse Poisson bivector computes \(\{f|_C,g|_C\}_{C}=\{f,g\}_D|_C\).
reconstruction: The restriction is nondegenerate because the constraints are second class, not merely because the ambient form is nondegenerate.
fate: This is the geometric content of the earlier reduction in \citet[\S8, pp.~138--140]{dirac1950generalized}; the notebook records Gelfand's explanatory intervention, not a new priority claim.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this intrinsic interpretation is standard.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Reduced equations and local canonical coordinates
notes: The multipliers are solved using \(Q^{-1}\); the reduced phase space has variables \(q^*,p^*\), a physical Hamiltonian and a reduced canonical one-form.
statement: For \(2m\) independent second-class constraints in a \(2n\)-dimensional phase space, the reduced space has dimension \(2(n-m)\). Hamilton's equations are \(\dot f=\{f,H\}_D|_C\), and Darboux coordinates exist locally on \(C\). The restricted canonical one-form differs from \(p^*dq^*\) by a locally exact form; an action equality therefore needs an endpoint term or fixed endpoint convention.
reconstruction: The number of constraints is made even in the ordinary bosonic case, and the exact differential omitted by the notes is restored.
fate: \citet[\S8, eqs.~(36)--(38)]{dirac1950generalized} gives the reduced bracket and dynamics. Its local canonical interpretation is classical; it asserts no global Darboux chart.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, regular local reduction is settled; global coordinates and singular strata are separate issues.

title: Canonical commutators and the limits of quantization
notes: The reduced variables are quantized by canonical (super)commutators, and \(\dot f\) is replaced by a commutator with the Hamiltonian.
statement: Canonical quantization prescribes the Heisenberg or Clifford relations for elementary even or odd variables and requires a representation, domains, ordering and a Hamiltonian operator. For a time-independent observable \(\widehat f\), \(\dot{\widehat f}=(i\hbar)^{-1}[\widehat f,\widehat H]\) in Heisenberg conventions. This does not imply a bracket-preserving quantization of every classical function.
reconstruction: The limitation prevents a universal quantization theorem from being read into a formal replacement rule.
fate: \citet[\S9, pp.~143--145]{dirac1950generalized} explicitly warns that the classical-to-operator correspondence is not uniquely defined because of ordering.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the elementary canonical algebra is standard; ordering, domains and consistency remain parts of each quantization problem.

title: Time-ordered source functional and Schwinger--Dyson equations
notes: Sources \(J,I\) couple to the reduced coordinates and momenta; time ordering and a source-dependent Hamiltonian generate functional differential equations.
statement: For a specified Hamiltonian operator, vacuum or boundary states and time-ordering convention, differentiating the source evolution operator yields time-ordered coordinate and momentum insertions. The operator equations of motion give functional Schwinger--Dyson relations, with contact terms at coincident times fixed by the ordering prescription.
reconstruction: States, contact terms and operator ordering are specified rather than inferred to be automatic.
fate: The functional-integral framework is reviewed in \citet[\S1]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}. The notebook itself explicitly flags the equal-time ordering issue; it is not resolved by writing a formal differential equation.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the formal source identities are standard; no convergence or unique time-slicing prescription is established here.

title: Phase-space functional Fourier representation
notes: The source equations are represented by an integral with phase \(\int(p^*\dot q^*-H_{\rm phys}+Jq^*+Ip^*)dt\); a margin discusses products at equal times.
statement: A time-sliced phase-space path integral can represent the evolution generated by a chosen ordered Hamiltonian, with discretization matched to its operator symbol. Different prescriptions can produce contact or ordering corrections. The continuous formula is shorthand for that chosen limit or for a formal perturbation series.
reconstruction: The symbol and discretization are additional data; the notebook's Fourier transform does not remove their necessity.
fate: \citet[\S5]{faddeevpopov1974gravity} derives the canonical functional-integral expression in the earlier gravity setting.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the representation is standard with a fixed prescription; the continuum integral is not a standalone definition for every Hamiltonian.

title: The second-class constraint measure
notes: The unreduced phase-space integral contains \(\delta(T)\sqrt{\operatorname{sdet}\{T,T\}}\).
statement: For regular second-class constraints \(T_\alpha\), the induced Liouville density can be represented in ambient coordinates by \(\delta(T)\sqrt{\det Q}\,dp\,dq\) in the ordinary even case, with an orientation or positive square-root convention. The super version uses the square root of the Berezinian and compatible odd delta conventions. The phase is the original Hamiltonian action restricted to the surface.
reconstruction: The local regular density identity and branch/orientation conditions are specified. This geometric measure identity is distinct from proving existence of the resulting oscillatory path integral.
fate: The ordinary construction is the publication lead \citet[pp.~227--261]{senjanovic1976path}; the graded extension is \citet[pp.~343--348]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}. Both predate the lecture. The original full texts were not recovered in this audit, so no internal equation locator or independently read proof is claimed.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular measure formula is standard; the notebook does not establish a nonperturbative measure or cover singular constraints.

title: Gauge fixing converts a regular first-class system to second class
notes: The first-class constraints are supplemented by gauge conditions \(\Phi_\alpha=0\); the combined bracket matrix is asserted to be nondegenerate.
statement: For \(m\) independent first-class constraints \(T_\alpha\), choose \(m\) local conditions \(\Phi_\alpha\) such that \(M_{\alpha\beta}=\{\Phi_\alpha,T_\beta\}|_{T=\Phi=0}\) is invertible. The combined \(2m\) constraints are then second class; on their surface the square root of the block determinant gives \(|\det M|\) in the bosonic positive-density convention. This realizes a local reduced phase-space integral.
reconstruction: The nonzero mixed determinant is a hypothesis, not a consequence of arbitrarily naming conditions a gauge. No global cross-section is promised.
fate: \citet[\S8]{dirac1950generalized} treats supplementary constraints; the path-integral determinant is part of \citet[\S5]{faddeevpopov1974gravity}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular local construction is established; Gribov copies and singular actions require further treatment.

title: The notebook's dilogarithm integral
notes: The displayed function is \(F(\xi)=\int_0^\xi\log x\,dx/(1-x)\).
statement: For \(0<\xi<1\), \(F(\xi)=-\log\xi\log(1-\xi)-\operatorname{Li}_2(\xi)=\operatorname{Li}_2(1-\xi)-\pi^2/6\). Thus this is a standard dilogarithmic variant, not the usual defining integral \(-\int_0^\xi\log(1-x)\,dx/x\) for \(\operatorname{Li}_2\). Complex continuation needs a domain and logarithm branches.
reconstruction: A real interval is chosen to make the literal integral and signs unambiguous; the equivalence follows by differentiation and the value at zero.
fate: The classical identities are reviewed in \citet[Chapter I, \S1]{zagier2007dilogarithm}; this later exposition does not imply a 2007 discovery.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the integral identity is elementary and settled.

title: The differential five-term relation needs related arguments
notes: The page writes \(\sum_{j=1}^5[\log u_j/(1-u_j)+\log(1-u_j)/u_j]du_j=0\), without relations among the five arguments.
statement: Set \(L(u)=\operatorname{Li}_2(u)+\tfrac12\log u\log(1-u)\). For \(0<x,y<1\), the five arguments \(x,y,(1-x)/(1-xy),1-xy,(1-y)/(1-xy)\) obey \(\sum L(u_j)=3L(1)=\pi^2/2\). Differentiating gives exactly the displayed one-form identity, since its summand is \(-2dL(u_j)\). It is false for five independently varying arguments.
reconstruction: The two-parameter substitution, range and branches are supplied; they cannot be recovered uniquely from the written equation alone.
fate: \citet[Chapter II, \S1.A, Rogers-dilogarithm five-term identity]{zagier2007dilogarithm} gives this precise classical identity.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected Rogers identity is established; the omitted relations are a source limitation.

title: Dilogarithms in algebraic K-theory
notes: The first entry is K-theory, with Bloch and Beilinson named.
statement: The following contribution supplies a concrete instance: a dilogarithmic primitive proves the Steinberg relation for the real regulator of \(K_2\) of a complex curve. This makes one precise connection, without interpreting the list as a theorem about every K-group.
reconstruction: The mathematical example is supplied from the immediately following talk; the introductory phrase has no independent quantifiers.
fate: \citet[\S1, Lemma 1 and the paragraph after it]{beilinson1980regulators} identifies the complex regulator and its real part, referring explicitly to Bloch's 1978 Irvine lectures. The lecture's precise construction is catalogued separately in record 476.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this connection is well established; the bare list does not identify a further theorem or open problem.

title: Combinatorial characteristic classes: the Gelfand--Gabrielov--Losik lead
notes: The second entry names combinatorial characteristic classes and the initials G.-G.-L.
statement: For a smooth manifold with a linearizable decomposition into simple cells satisfying the configuration-space connectivity condition (A), the Gelfand--Gabrielov--Losik construction produces a rational codimension-four cycle Poincar\'e dual to the first Pontryagin class. A real dilogarithmic variant enters this combinatorial construction. The notebook does not specify its normalization or a formula for a higher characteristic class.
reconstruction: This is a literature-supported identification of the named connection, with the original theorem's hypotheses retained. The source does not record enough to choose the dilogarithm's normalization or infer a new general characteristic-class claim.
fate: The precise cycle theorem is \citet[\S1, Proposition 10 and Theorem 1, Russian p.~18]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1975computation}, published in 1975; receipt on 2 December 1974 is not a verified public circulation date. The later local formulation is \citet[Theorems 1--3]{gabrielovgelfandlosik1976local}. \citet[\S3, pp.~115--116]{goncharov1993classical} explicitly identifies the dilogarithmic ingredient in the 1975 construction.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the named connection is established and predates the talk; no additional conjecture is recoverable from the list.

title: Hyperbolic tetrahedral volume
notes: The third entry mentions the volume of a non-Euclidean tetrahedron and Gauss.
statement: For an oriented ideal hyperbolic tetrahedron whose vertices on the sphere at infinity have cross-ratio \(z\), its signed volume is \(D(z)=\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(z)+\log|z|\arg(1-z)\). Orientation reversal changes the sign. A general finite tetrahedron needs a more elaborate formula.
reconstruction: Ideal vertices, orientation and cross-ratio are additional specifications. The source's unqualified tetrahedron is not silently identified with this special case.
fate: \citet[Chapter I, \S4, eq.~(4.1)]{zagier2007dilogarithm} states the ideal-tetrahedron formula and its classical historical setting. This is a precise special case of the notebook's broad reference; no priority claim for Gauss alone is inferred.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the ideal-volume identity is established; this page does not select a general tetrahedral-volume formula.

title: Apéry's zeta(3) result and an unspecified dilogarithm link
notes: The fourth entry is simply \(\zeta(3)\), with Apéry's name.
statement: Apéry's theorem asserts \(\zeta(3)\notin\mathbb Q\). The notebook gives no integral, recurrence, special-value identity or reduction of that theorem to a dilogarithm; those are not reconstructed as an additional claim.
reconstruction: The established theorem and the unidentified link are deliberately separated.
fate: \citet[pp.~11--13]{apery1979irrationalite} is the primary 1979 publication from the 1978 arithmetic meeting. It confirms the irrationality result but does not identify the particular dilogarithmic connection intended by this list.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, Apéry's irrationality theorem is settled; the content of the listed connection is not sufficiently specified to classify as an open problem.

title: Web geometry and Bol
notes: The fifth entry names webs and Bol, with no formula or web specified.
statement: The classical Bol five-web is the germ, at a generic point of \(\mathbb C^2\), of the foliations with first integrals \(x,y,x/y,(1-y)/(1-x),x(1-y)/(y(1-x))\). It has six independent Abelian relations, the maximal rank for a planar five-web, and is not locally equivalent to an algebraic web. The additional relation beyond those generated by three-subwebs is the dilogarithmic five-term identity.
reconstruction: The particular web and its generic-point hypothesis come from the checked literature. This is a strong identification of the named example, not evidence that all of its hypotheses or rank claims were spoken in the seminar.
fate: \citet[\S6.1.4, p.~190; introduction p.~6]{pereirapirio2009web} states the foliations and relation and gives the nonalgebraizability argument; its bibliography attributes the example to Bol's 1936 paper. The original 1936 proof was not separately recovered. This explicit older result identifies the named connection, without converting the notebook list into a classification problem.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, Bol's exceptional web is established; the entry records no definite new open question.

title: Scattering theory: an unqualified connection
notes: A sixth entry in the right margin reads scattering theory.
statement: No scattering equation, dimension, observable, loop order or dilogarithmic identity is stated. Consequently the remark has no determinate mathematical proposition beyond suggesting an area of application.
fate: Primary-source searches combining dilogarithms with scattering and amplitudes yield many inequivalent applications. None can be designated the fate of this particular remark without a model or formula.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the intended application remains unidentified; no open scattering problem is manufactured from the label.

title: The zeta(2) integral has a missing minus sign
notes: Equation (3) states \(\int_0^1\log x\,dx/(1-x)=\sum 1/n^2\), with no visible minus sign in the scan.
statement: The correct identity is \(\int_0^1\log x\,dx/(1-x)=-\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-2}=-\pi^2/6\). Expanding \((1-x)^{-1}\) and applying monotone convergence to the nonnegative function \(-\log x/(1-x)\) justifies termwise integration.
reconstruction: The lower limit on the sum and the minus sign are supplied; the elementary justification is editorial.
fate: This is a classical dilogarithm evaluation; compare \citet[Chapter I, \S1]{zagier2007dilogarithm}. Its sign is also forced by the negative integrand on \((0,1)\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected identity is settled; both transcriptions faithfully retain the notebook's sign error.

title: Bloch's proposed replacement of zeta(2) by a curve zeta function
notes: The introduction says generalization to curves, names Bloch, and replaces the right-hand zeta value by the curve's zeta function.
statement: No base number field, arithmetic model, value of the complex parameter, order of vanishing, regulator determinant or rational factor is recorded. There is therefore no uniquely recoverable special-value formula or conjecture.
fate: \citet[\S1 and bibliography item 1]{beilinson1980regulators} explicitly relates the real regulator to Bloch's 1978 Irvine lectures. Its later \S2 concerns higher regulators and L-values, but that is not evidence that all those conjectural quantifiers were stated here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the historical regulator context is identifiable; the vague zeta remark remains unsuitable for an independent problem record.

title: A closed real regulator one-form
notes: For nowhere-zero holomorphic functions on a Riemann surface the notes define \(\omega_{f,g}=\log|f|d\arg g-\log|g|d\arg f\) and infer that integration along paths is well defined.
statement: On a Riemann surface where \(f,g\) are holomorphic units, \(d\arg f=\operatorname{Im}(df/f)\) is globally defined and \(d\omega_{f,g}=0\). Hence its integrals depend only on the relative homology class of a path with fixed endpoints; closedness does not assert independence of every path between those endpoints.
reconstruction: The global one-form is distinguished from a globally chosen argument function; path homotopy or homology is the required qualification.
fate: The real regulator is attributed to Bloch's 1978 lectures in \citet[\S1, paragraph following Lemma 1]{beilinson1980regulators}. The displayed differential identity also follows directly from the Cauchy--Riemann equations.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the closed-form construction is established; nonzero periods are precisely part of its regulator content.

title: Bilinearity and alternation of the real regulator form
notes: Equations (6)--(7) give additivity in a product of functions and antisymmetry under interchanging them.
statement: For holomorphic units, \(\omega_{f_1f_2,g}=\omega_{f_1,g}+\omega_{f_2,g}\), \(\omega_{f,g_1g_2}=\omega_{f,g_1}+\omega_{f,g_2}\), and \(\omega_{g,f}=-\omega_{f,g}\). These are equalities of differential forms, not merely of cohomology classes.
fate: These elementary identities underlie Bloch's real regulator, recalled by \citet[\S1]{beilinson1980regulators}; they are already implicit in the logarithmic formula.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the identities are exact on the common domain of invertibility.

title: The single-valued dilogarithm proves the Steinberg relation
notes: The form \(\omega_{f,1-f}\) is asserted to be exact. Equation (9) writes its primitive using a logarithm term and the imaginary part of an integral, and emphasizes single-valuedness.
statement: The Bloch--Wigner dilogarithm \(D(z)=\operatorname{Im}\operatorname{Li}_2(z)+\log|z|\arg(1-z)\) is single valued on \(\mathbb C\setminus\{0,1\}\), extends continuously by zero at \(0,1,\infty\), and satisfies \(dD(z)=\log|z|d\arg(1-z)-\log|1-z|d\arg z\). Consequently \(\omega_{f,1-f}=d(D\circ f)\) whenever \(f,1-f\) are holomorphic units.
reconstruction: Individual logarithms and the complex dilogarithm require local branches; their stated combination is the global function. The lower endpoint zero is understood by its continuous limit.
fate: \citet[Chapter I, \S3]{zagier2007dilogarithm} records the precise single-valued function and differential. The pre-1979 Bloch regulator context is confirmed in \citet[\S1]{beilinson1980regulators}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this exactness identity and hence the real Steinberg relation are established.

title: David Wigner and continuous cohomology of SL(2)
notes: The notebook attributes the single-valued function to D. Wigner and says he connected it to continuous cohomology of \(SL(2)\).
statement: Fix \(x\in\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\). On generic quadruples set \(c_x(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3)=D(\operatorname{cr}(g_0x,g_1x,g_2x,g_3x))\). The five-term identity makes this a homogeneous measurable real three-cocycle for \(GL_2(\mathbb C)\), restricting to \(SL_2(\mathbb C)\); it represents the nonzero degree-three volume class under the measurable/continuous cohomology comparison. Changing \(x\) gives a cohomologous cocycle.
reconstruction: The complex group, real coefficients, degree, generic quadruples and comparison map are supplied from the literature. This identifies a standard precise version of the note; the notebook itself suppresses these data.
fate: \citet[\S3, p.~117, eqs.~(10)--(12)]{goncharov1993classical} explicitly attributes this construction to Wigner and places it in the 1970s. The 1993 chapter is the checked exposition, not the first-circulation date of Wigner's observation; no original Wigner preprint date was verified.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the volume-cocycle interpretation is established; the source's omission of field and degree is recorded rather than treated as an open problem.

title: A puncture period and the tame symbol
notes: Equation (10) equates a small-loop integral of \(\omega_{f,g}\) with \(\log|f^{v_x(g)}/g^{v_x(f)}|(x)\), without a factor \(2\pi\).
statement: Let \(f=z^m a(z)\), \(g=z^n b(z)\) near \(x\), with \(a(0)b(0)\ne0\). For a positively oriented small circle \(\gamma_x\), \(\int_{\gamma_x}\omega_{f,g}=2\pi\log|a(0)^n/b(0)^m|=2\pi\log|\partial_x\{f,g\}|\), where \(\partial_x\{f,g\}=(-1)^{mn}a(0)^n/b(0)^m\).
reconstruction: Orientation, local expansions and the tame sign are specified. The tame sign disappears under absolute value but not in the later complex symbol.
fate: The complex local tame-symbol identity is \citet[\S1, Lemma 1(b)]{beilinson1980regulators}; taking logarithmic absolute values gives the corrected real normalization.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected period identity is exact. The missing factor is a faithful notebook error, not a translation issue.

title: Symbols present K2 of the function field, not automatically of the curve
notes: The notes quotient symbols by bimultiplicativity, antisymmetry and the Steinberg relation, then call the result both \(K_2(X)\) and K2 of its rational function field.
statement: For a field \(F\), Matsumoto's theorem identifies Quillen \(K_2(F)\) with the abelian group on \(\{f,g\}\), \(f,g\in F^\times\), subject to bimultiplicativity and \(\{f,1-f\}=0\) for \(f\ne0,1\). Skew symmetry follows from these relations. Taking \(F=\mathbb C(X)\) defines the function-field group; it does not by itself define \(K_2(X)\).
reconstruction: The ambient free group is made abelian, and the curve and function-field notation are separated.
fate: The result dates to Matsumoto's 1969 theorem, stated precisely in \citet[III.6.1]{weibel2013kbook}. The notebook's Milnor/Steinberg attribution is compatible with this older framework.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the field presentation is established; the missing passage to the curve is supplied by localization in the following item.

title: The unique smooth projective completion of an algebraic curve
notes: A parenthesis says an algebraic curve is compactified uniquely, for example by embedding it in projective space and taking the closure.
statement: A smooth connected algebraic curve over \(\mathbb C\) has a smooth projective completion unique up to the unique isomorphism extending the given open curve. The normalization of a projective closure gives that smooth completion. A raw projective closure can be singular; arbitrary open Riemann surfaces need not be algebraic or of finite type.
reconstruction: Smoothness, algebraicity, normalization and uniqueness relative to the given open immersion are the missing hypotheses. The preceding general Riemann surface is not silently assumed algebraic.
fate: This is the classical smooth-curve model used in the regulator construction of \citet[\S1]{beilinson1980regulators}; it is not a new theorem announced by this talk.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected completion statement is standard; the unrestricted topological or analytic reading is false.

title: Localization and extension of the real regulator over punctures
notes: Equation (12) writes \(K_2(X)\to K_2(\mathbb C(X))\to\bigoplus_x\mathbb C^*\). A sum of symbols with trivial local terms then gives a class in \(H^1(X,\mathbb R)\).
statement: For a smooth algebraic curve, localization identifies the image of \(K_2(X)\to K_2(\mathbb C(X))\) with the kernel of the sum of tame symbols. If \(\xi=\sum_i n_i\{f_i,g_i\}\) has trivial tame symbol at every point of \(X\), the closed form \(\sum_i n_i\omega_{f_i,g_i}\), initially off its divisors, has zero small-loop periods and determines a unique class in \(H^1(X,\mathbb R)\). This defines the real regulator on \(K_2(X)\) by composition.
reconstruction: The statement concerns an image/kernel exactness assertion. The notes do not supply a proof of injectivity of the first arrow, and no such assertion is needed for the regulator construction. Uniqueness is uniqueness of the extended cohomology class, not of an arbitrary differential form.
fate: \citet[\S1, immediately after Lemma 1]{beilinson1980regulators} explicitly uses Quillen's localization theorem and identifies the resulting logarithmic absolute value with Bloch's regulator, already circulated in his 1978 lectures.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular-curve regulator construction is established; it makes no special-value conjecture without further arithmetic data.

title: Beilinson's complex multiplicative regulator
notes: Equation (16) defines an exponentiated logarithmic integral in cases according to the winding number of \(g\), with a sign \((-1)^{v_\gamma(f)v_\gamma(g)}\). The symbol is said to be bimultiplicative, symmetric and Steinberg, and to recover the real construction.
statement: For a loop \(\gamma\) based at \(a\), avoid the divisors and continue chosen logarithms along the loop. A convenient equivalent formula is \[r_\gamma(f,g)=\exp\!\left[\frac{1}{2\pi i}\left(\int_\gamma\log f\,d\log g-\log g(a)\int_\gamma d\log f\right)\right].\] It is independent of the initial logarithm choices, homotopy invariant, bimultiplicative, multiplicatively skew, and satisfies \(r_\gamma(f,1-f)=1\). On a puncture circle it is the tame symbol. Moreover \(\log|r_\gamma(f,g)|=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_\gamma\omega_{f,g}\), so unramified symbols yield the complex refinement of the real regulator.
reconstruction: The basepoint formula makes branch normalization explicit and avoids the notebook's case division. Multiplicative skew symmetry means \(r_\gamma(g,f)=r_\gamma(f,g)^{-1}\); literal symmetry would generally be false. Taking logarithmic absolute value, with the stated factor, is the recovery of the real regulator.
fate: This is an exact construction match to \citet[\S1, eq.~(1) and Lemma 1]{beilinson1980regulators}, published in 1980. The journal records receipt on 21 December 1979; no earlier public preprint date was verified. The notebook documents the seminar on 19 November 1979. The paper also acknowledges an independent unpublished construction by Deligne.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this regulator refinement was published soon after the seminar and is established. It is not merely a retrospective thematic link to later Beilinson conjectures.

title: Stable Steinberg extension and second group homology
notes: For an affine curve the notes write \(K_2(X)=H_2(SL_n(A),\mathbb Z)\) and \(1\to K_2(X)\to St^X\to SL^X\to1\), where \(A\) is its ring of algebraic functions.
statement: For a unital ring \(A\), the stable Steinberg group gives the universal central extension \(1\to K_2(A)\to\operatorname{St}(A)\to E(A)\to1\), and \(K_2(A)\cong H_2(E(A),\mathbb Z)\). If \(X=\operatorname{Spec}A\), its algebraic K2 is \(K_2(A)\). Replacing the stable elementary group by a particular \(SL_n(A)\) requires both the relevant equality with the elementary group and homology/K2 stability hypotheses.
reconstruction: The stable rank and elementary-group qualifications are essential. They are supplied rather than choosing an unjustified finite rank for the source.
fate: The Kervaire--Steinberg theorem is stated in \citet[III.5.5; stability discussion III.5.5.2]{weibel2013kbook}, which traces the older Milnor/Steinberg theory. It does not assert the displayed equality for arbitrary \(n\).
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the stable statement is established; the source's unspecified finite-rank formulation is not a complete theorem.

title: Promoting Lagrange multipliers to canonical variables
notes: The multiplier \(\lambda\) is paired with a momentum \(\pi\), and the extended constraints are \(G_a=(\pi_\mu,T_\mu)\). Gauge conditions include \(-\dot\lambda^\mu+\chi^\mu\). The count is \((n+m)-2m=n-m\).
statement: For a regular irreducible bosonic system with \(n\) canonical pairs and \(m\) independent first-class constraints, add \(m\) multiplier pairs. The extended phase space has dimension \(2(n+m)\), and its \(2m\) first-class constraints, when regularly reduced, leave dimension \(2(n-m)\). Differential gauge conditions for the multipliers can be encoded by a suitable extended Hamiltonian. This is a local degree-of-freedom count, not a proof that arbitrary gauges are admissible.
reconstruction: The count refers to independent regular bosonic constraints. The overwritten sign and momentum index in source equation (4) are not silently repaired; the clear equations (6)--(7) determine the construction.
fate: The contemporaneous publication leads are \citet[pp.~309--312]{batalinvilkovisky1977relativistic} and \citet[pp.~343--348]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization}. The later Hamiltonian framework is explicitly described in \citet[introduction and \S~II]{bering1997geometry}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular extended-phase-space construction is established; the literal ambiguous formula (4) remains a transcription uncertainty.

title: Ghost canonical pairs and the BFV phase-space action
notes: Equation (8) integrates \((q^A,p_A,\eta^a,\mathcal P_a)\) with phase \(\int(p_A\dot q^A+\mathcal P_a\dot\eta^a-H_{\rm complete})dt\).
statement: For each constraint \(G_a\), introduce a ghost \(\eta^a\) of opposite parity and its conjugate momentum \(\mathcal P_a\), with ghost numbers \(+1\) and \(-1\). The full symplectic structure is even. With a chosen time-slicing, boundary states and integration prescription the displayed phase-space expression is the formal BFV partition functional.
reconstruction: Ghost number, parity and boundary prescriptions are supplied. Odd ghost variables do not make the ambient Poisson bracket odd, and no BV antifields have been introduced.
fate: The boson/fermion extension belongs to the 1977/1978 Hamiltonian publications just cited. \citet[\S~II and \S~V.2, eq.~(V.8)]{bering1997geometry} writes the later precise geometric version and states its assumptions.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, this is the standard Hamiltonian ghost extension; the displayed continuum integral remains formal without further analytic construction.

title: Nilpotent Hamiltonian charge, invariant Hamiltonian and gauge fermion
notes: Equations (9)--(11) require \(\{\Omega,\Omega\}=0\), \(\{H_1,\Omega\}=0\), and \(H_{\rm complete}=H_1-\{\Psi,\Omega\}\), with \(\Psi=\mathcal P_a\chi^a\).
statement: Let the odd charge \(\Omega\) have ghost number one and satisfy the even-bracket master equation \(\{\Omega,\Omega\}=0\). Let \(H_1\) be even, ghost number zero, and BRST invariant. For any admissible odd gauge fermion \(\Psi\) of ghost number minus one, the displayed gauge-fixed Hamiltonian is again BRST invariant by the graded Jacobi identity.
reconstruction: Parities and ghost numbers make the equations precise; the sign of the gauge-fixing term is conventional once \(\Psi\) is fixed.
fate: \citet[\S~II, eq.~(II.6), and \S~V.2]{bering1997geometry} gives this Hamiltonian structure and attributes it to the earlier BFV work. The original 1977/1978 articles are indirect publication checks, not a claim that the 1979 notes anticipated the later Lagrangian BV formalism.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the algebraic BRST-invariance statement is exact; admissibility and quantum gauge independence require the additional hypotheses in item 1979-478.7.

title: Solving the Hamiltonian BRST equations as a formal series
notes: The speaker says the equations for \(\Omega\) and \(H_1\) can be solved as series in ghosts and ghost momenta whenever the constraints are first class.
statement: For a regular irreducible first-class constraint system, with the usual acyclic constraint resolution locally, one can recursively construct a formal charge beginning \(\Omega=\eta^aG_a+\cdots\) and a BRST extension of a Hamiltonian preserving the constraints. Reducible systems need further ghosts; singular constraints need additional hypotheses. Formal solvability asserts neither convergence nor finite termination.
reconstruction: Regularity, irreducibility or a suitable resolution, locality and formality are necessary additions to the notebook's all-first-class wording.
fate: \citet[pp.~343--348]{fradkinfradkina1978quantization} is the contemporaneous graded-constraint publication lead. \citet[introduction]{bering1997geometry} confirms the later BFV framework but assumes, rather than proves, the existence of the charge used in that article. The original recursive proof was not recovered here.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the regular formal existence framework is established; an unrestricted singular-system theorem is not verified by the notes or the checked publication text.

title: Termination of the supergravity ghost expansion
notes: The series are said usually to terminate in supergravity.
statement: A finite ghost-degree bound depends on the particular supergravity theory, formulation, auxiliary fields and constraint generators. None is specified, so the word usually does not define a universal termination theorem.
fate: The contemporary modified-rule lead is \citet[pp.~141--152]{kallosh1978modified}. The later open-algebra discussion in \citet[\S2.2]{fuster2005brst} confirms the relevant phenomenon but supplies no model-independent bound matching this phrase.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, model-specific constructions exist; this notebook remark remains too imprecise for a separate open-problem identifier.

title: Hamiltonian BRST transformations and nilpotence
notes: Equation (12) writes \(\delta X=\{X,\Omega\}\mu\), with \(\mu\) an odd constant.
statement: The differential \(sX=\{X,\Omega\}\), with a consistent right/left derivation convention, has odd parity and satisfies \(s^2=0\) when \(\{\Omega,\Omega\}=0\). A constant odd parameter gives an even infinitesimal change of integration variables. The symplectic potential changes by an endpoint term, so invariance of an action also depends on boundary conditions.
reconstruction: Nilpotence is a property of the odd derivation itself, not merely a vacuous consequence of the square of one Grassmann parameter being zero.
fate: \citet[\S~II, eq.~(II.6), and \S~V.2, eq.~(V.9)]{bering1997geometry} displays the nilpotent charge and the endpoint condition in the Hamiltonian setting.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the algebraic identity is exact, with boundary conditions needed for the integrated action.

title: Field-dependent BRST change of variables and gauge independence
notes: The last formula chooses \(\mu=i\int\mathcal P_a\,\delta\chi^a\,dt\) and concludes BRST invariance.
statement: For an infinitesimal change of an admissible gauge fermion, a BRST change of path variables with a field-dependent odd parameter can compensate the change of gauge-fixing action through its Jacobian. This proves formal gauge independence only when the measure is BRST compatible, boundary terms vanish, the gauges are connected without a singularity, and no global orbit obstruction has been ignored.
reconstruction: A field-dependent parameter does not generate an ordinary canonical transformation with unit Jacobian. The Jacobian, rather than constant-parameter invariance alone, is the crucial missing step.
fate: \citet[\S~II, \S~V.2 and \S~V.3]{bering1997geometry} analyzes precisely this field-dependent path-space change and states explicitly that global Gribov problems, phase-space boundaries and existence of the path integral are excluded or assumed. Its arXiv preprint first circulated in September 1997; the mechanism itself is attributed there to the original BFV work.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the qualified formal BFV theorem is established; the notes do not prove a global, nonperturbative gauge-independence theorem.

title: First-generation charges and valence nucleon diagrams
notes: The diagrams pair \((\nu,e)\) and \((u,d)\), assign charges \((0,-1)\) and \((2/3,-1/3)\), and draw proton \(uud\) and neutron \(udd\).
statement: In units of the positron charge, the first-generation charge eigenvalues are \(Q(\nu_e)=0\), \(Q(e)=-1\), \(Q(u)=2/3\), \(Q(d)=-1/3\). The valence assignments give \(Q(uud)=1\) and \(Q(udd)=0\). The valence picture does not assert that a physical nucleon has only three constituents and no gluon or sea-quark degrees of freedom.
reconstruction: The scan's circles are interpreted as valence diagrams, and charge eigenvalues are distinguished from an identity matrix acting on a doublet.
fate: These are pre-1979 quark-model and electroweak assignments. Their current representation conventions are stated in \citet[\S10.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak}; the QCD field content is given in \citet[\S9.1]{hustonrabbertzzanderighi2026qcd}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, these charge assignments remain standard; the schematic nucleon drawing is not a full wavefunction.

title: Colour triplets, singlets and eight adjoint gluons
notes: Each quark is tripled into colour components, \(SU(3)_c\) acts by a unitary matrix, leptons are not tripled, and eight gluons are identified with the adjoint representation.
statement: Each quark flavour transforms in the fundamental \(\mathbf3\) of \(SU(3)_c\); leptons are colour singlets. The gauge connection takes values in \(\mathfrak{su}(3)\), whose dimension is eight, and its homogeneous colour rotation is adjoint. A local gauge transformation of the connection also has an inhomogeneous derivative term.
reconstruction: The ambiguous adjoint annotation on P000890 is attached to the gauge field as clarified on P000892; it is not used to place quarks in the eight-dimensional adjoint representation.
fate: \citet[\S9.1, eq.~(9.1) and its definitions]{hustonrabbertzzanderighi2026qcd} states the QCD representation and curvature conventions. This is confirmation of the older framework, not a later resolution of a seminar conjecture.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the representation distinction is established and unchanged.

title: Chiral weak doublets, singlets and hypercharge
notes: The weak group mixes each doublet synchronously and is written \(SU(2)\times U(1)\) on P000891, but \(SU(2)\times SU(1)\) on P000892. The right electron is called a singlet under the displayed product.
statement: With \(Q=T_3+Y\), the lepton representations are \(L_L=(\nu_L,e_L)\sim(\mathbf2,-1/2)\) and \(e_R\sim(\mathbf1,-1)\) under \(SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y\). The right electron is a singlet only of the \(SU(2)\) factor. Gauge transformations are continuous linear transformations, not merely permutations of particle labels. The minimal model has no right-handed neutrino field.
reconstruction: The Abelian group and nontrivial right-electron hypercharge are restored. Spontaneous symmetry breaking, rather than unequal masses by themselves, explains why the vacuum need not exhibit the whole weak symmetry.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{weinberg1967leptons} gives the earlier chiral model; \citet[\S10.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak} states modern normalizations.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the corrected representation assignment is standard; a right-electron singlet of the entire product would have zero electric charge.

title: Dirac matrices, chirality and the massless limit
notes: The talk writes the Dirac equation, the Clifford anticommutator and chiral projectors. Its displayed \(\gamma^5\) has the opposite sign to one common convention, so the projector labeled left is \((1+\gamma^5)/2\).
statement: For \(\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}\) and \(\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)\), choose \(\gamma^5\) with \((\gamma^5)^2=1\) and \(\{\gamma^5,\gamma^\mu\}=0\). Then \(P_\pm=(1\pm\gamma^5)/2\) are complementary projectors. The massless Dirac equation separates into two Weyl equations; a mass term couples them. For positive-energy massless particles chirality matches helicity after fixing conventions, but for massive particles they are distinct notions.
reconstruction: The sign of \(\gamma^5\) is treated as a convention, not a transcription mistake. A four-component notation for a Weyl neutrino does not decide whether actual massive neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana.
fate: The chiral lepton construction is already used in \citet[eqs.~(1)--(4)]{weinberg1967leptons}. \citet[\S14.1]{gonzalezgarciawendell2026neutrinos} distinguishes the massless minimal model from the observed neutrino-mixing framework.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the Clifford and projection identities are exact; the notebook's massless-neutrino assumption is a historical model assumption.

title: Photon, charged-current and neutral-current exchange
notes: Feynman sketches show photon, \(W^-\) and \(Z^0\) exchange. The photon is massless, the weak bosons massive, and approximate mass predictions are labeled about \(85m_p\) and \(95m_p\).
statement: In the electroweak model a massless photon couples to the electromagnetic charge current, charged \(W^\pm\) bosons couple the two left-handed components of weak doublets, and a neutral \(Z\) couples to a weak neutral current. Gauge-boson lines in a perturbative diagram represent propagators carrying four-momentum. The 1979 masses are model predictions and rough numerical estimates, not measurements supplied by the source.
reconstruction: The diagram's particle labels are read as examples of the interaction vertices; no exact cross section or claim of experimental discovery in 1979 is inferred.
fate: \citet[eqs.~(5)--(14)]{weinberg1967leptons} derives the earlier mass and current structure. Current measured masses and electroweak fits are treated in \citet[\S10.4.1]{deblasdittmaierkogler2026electroweak}.
present_status: As of 10 November 2026, the weak gauge bosons are experimentally established; detailed current couplings and the tree-level mass relation are reconstructed in record 480.
